title: The complete Nile cruise guide
standfirst: Everything to decide before a Nile cruise: which route, which time of year, how many nights and how to plan around flights and sightseeing. Start with the route; the rest follows.

sections.heading: The short version
paragraphs: Most Nile cruises sail between Luxor and Aswan: four nights upstream from Luxor or three nights downstream from Aswan. Dahabiyas often sail between Esna and Aswan over four or five nights. October to April is cooler and busier; summer is hot and quieter.

sections.heading: How a cruise day works
paragraphs: Sightseeing starts early, before the heat. Afternoons are spent sailing, and evenings on board. A cruise runs from check-in on the first day to check-out on the last, so plan flights and transfers around those times.

sections.heading: Choosing a boat
paragraphs: The vessel shapes the trip more than anything else. Our guide to the three types of Nile boat explains the differences.

faqs.q: How long is a Nile cruise?
faqs.a: Usually three or four nights between Luxor and Aswan, and four or five on a dahabiya. Longer cruises exist but are rare.
Most cruises include guided visits. A private Egyptologist is available on many cruises at extra cost.
